methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches AI training program for workplace professionals - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's workplace AI training program represents distributed capability-building outside major metros, signaling potential for peer-to-peer learning networks that could spread deep AI fluency beyond the NoVA-Richmond corridor.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's partnership with AI Ready RVA explicitly targets community-wide AI education and innovation, suggesting institutional commitment to distributed depth rather than elite concentration—a potential countervailing force to the NoVA gravity well.

signals.title: Digital Realty Acquires $7.8 bn Northern Virginia Data Center Portfolio from Blackstone to Expand AI Infrastructure - InfotechLead
signals.signal_reading: Digital Realty's $7.8B data center acquisition consolidates AI infrastructure investment in NoVA, reinforcing the region's computational advantage while physical infrastructure remains geographically locked, deepening metro-rural capability asymmetry.

signals.title: Virginia county asks all employees, including schools, to conserve power due to AI-driven electricity price hikes — state's 400-plus data centers steadily increasing demand, grid expansion, and pricing - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: County-wide power conservation requests due to data center electricity demand reveals how AI infrastructure concentration creates resource scarcity for public institutions, potentially constraining distributed capability development through basic infrastructure limits.

signals.title: AI Has Already Arrived in Roanoke’s Classrooms. Here’s What Parents, Students, and Workers Should Know. - The Roanoke Rambler
signals.signal_reading: AI's arrival in Roanoke classrooms through platform tools suggests shallow but distributed adoption—students gain access to AI capabilities without necessarily developing deep technical fluency or algorithmic understanding.
